column1: 配線の見た目と作りやすさを整える
column2: Tidy up how tracks look and how easy they are to make

column1: 配線の角を丸め、太さが変わる所をなめらかにし、2本が合流する所のすき間を銅で埋めます。製造のとき、エッチングで細いすき間がつぶれたり、液がたまったりするのを防ぎます
column2: Rounds track corners, smooths places where the width changes, and fills the gaps where two tracks meet with copper. This keeps thin gaps from closing up or trapping liquid during etching at the fab

column1: 基板エディタの「仕上げ (任意)」
column2: Finishing (optional) in the board editor

column1: 配線の太さを、流れる電流から決める
column2: Choose track width from the current

column1: 回路の電流から、配線に必要な太さを求め、電圧降下 (配線の抵抗で電圧が下がる量) も確かめます
column2: Finds the track width the circuit's current needs, and also checks the voltage drop (how much the voltage falls because of the track's resistance)

column1: 基板エディタの「③ 確認して発注」の「電流と電圧降下」
column2: Current and voltage drop under "③ Check and order" in the board editor

column1: 差動ペアと長さ合わせ
column2: Differential pairs and length matching

column1: USB のように2本で信号を送る線を並べて引き、長さをそろえます。高い周波数の信号が乱れにくくなります
column2: Routes two-wire signal lines such as USB side by side and makes them the same length. High-frequency signals are then less easily disturbed

column1: 同じ「高度な配線 (中級者向け)」の「差動ペア」「長さ合わせ (蛇行)」
column2: Differential pairs and "Length matching (meander)" in the same "Advanced routing (intermediate)"

column1: 発注と、買うものの一覧
column2: Ordering, and a list of what to buy

column1: ガーバー・ドリル・部品表・配置ファイルと一緒に、部品ごとの数量と、秋月電子・DigiKey・LCSC のリンク (型番が分かる部品は商品ページ) を書き出します
column2: Along with the Gerber, drill, BOM and placement files, writes out the quantity of each part and links to Akizuki Denshi, DigiKey and LCSC (product pages for parts whose part number is known)

column1: 基板エディタの「③ 確認して発注」の「発注の準備…」
column2: Prepare order… under "③ Check and order" in the board editor

column1: 部品の故障を試す
column2: Try part faults

column1: 抵抗が焼ける、コンデンサがショートするなど、部品が壊れたときに回路がどうなるか、ほかの部品が連鎖して壊れないかを調べます
column2: Checks what happens to the circuit when a part breaks, such as a resistor burning out or a capacitor shorting, and whether other parts break in a chain

column1: 回路図の左パネルの「故障を試す」「連鎖故障を追う」
column2: Try fault and "Follow cascading faults" in the schematic's left panel

column1: 部品の誤差と温度の影響
column2: Effects of part tolerances and temperature

column1: 抵抗やコンデンサの誤差、温度の変化で、出力がどれだけ動くかを、たくさんの組み合わせで調べます
column2: Checks with many combinations how much the output moves with resistor and capacitor tolerances and temperature changes

column1: 回路図の左パネルの「ばらつき解析を実行」「温度スイープを実行」
column2: Run tolerance analysis and "Run temperature sweep" in the schematic's left panel

column1: ほかのソフトと行き来する
column2: Working with other software

column1: 回路を SPICE のネットリストで書き出して LTspice や ngspice で動かしたり、KiCad の部品を取り込んだり、自分で部品を作って足したりできます
column2: You can export the circuit as a SPICE netlist to run it in LTspice or ngspice, import KiCad parts, and create and add your own parts

column1: 回路図の左パネルの「SPICEネットリストを書き出し…」「＋ 部品を作る…」(開いた窓の「① 基本」に、KiCad・JSON から取り込むボタンがあります)
column2: SPICE export… and "+ Create part…" in the schematic's left panel (the "① Basics" tab of the window that opens has buttons to import from KiCad and JSON)

column1: 画面なしで動かす (ccad)
column2: Run without a screen (ccad)

column1: 1行1コマンドのスクリプトで、回路づくりから解析・基板・製造データまでを自動で実行します。AI エージェントから使うこともできます
column2: Runs everything automatically from building the circuit to analysis, the board and fab data, with a script of one command per line. AI agents can use it too

column1: ソフトに付いてくる `ccad`。使い方は docs/cli.md
column2: `ccad`, which comes with the software. Usage is in docs/cli.md

column1: # crates/app/src/learn/paths.rs
トランジスタのスイッチ
column2: Transistor switch

column1: ベース電流でコレクタ電流を制御する。電流を増やす部品の入口
column2: The base current controls the collector current. A first look at parts that amplify current

column1: トランジスタで LED をオン・オフし、ベース電流とコレクタ電流を測ります
column2: Turn an LED on and off with a transistor, and measure the base and collector currents

column1: 電池の内部抵抗 (負荷で電圧が下がる)
column2: Battery internal resistance (voltage drops under load)

column1: 電源の電圧が、電流を流すと下がる。これを小さくするのが安定化電源の役目
column2: A supply's voltage drops when current flows. Keeping this small is the job of a regulated supply

column1: 電池に抵抗をつないで、つなぐ前後の端子電圧を測り、内部抵抗を求めます
column2: Connect a resistor to a battery, measure the terminal voltage before and after, and find the internal resistance

column1: 電源を守る (逆接続・過電流・ヒューズ)
column2: Protecting the supply (reverse polarity, overcurrent, fuses)

column1: 壊れ方を知って、守る部品を足す
column2: Learn how things fail, and add protection parts

column1: ヒューズや逆接続保護ダイオードの働きを、安全な条件 (低電圧・電流制限つき) で確かめます
column2: Check how fuses and reverse-polarity protection diodes work under safe conditions (low voltage, current-limited)

column1: LDO (低ドロップアウト) レギュレータ
column2: LDO (low-dropout) regulator

column1: 入力の余裕 (ドロップアウト電圧) が小さくても動く。USB の 5V や電池から 3.3V を作る。電圧差は熱になる
column2: Works even with little input headroom (dropout voltage). Makes 3.3V from USB 5V or a battery. The voltage difference turns into heat

column1: 入力を下げながら出力を測り、出力が落ち始める入力を、データシートと比べます
column2: Lower the input while measuring the output, find the input where the output starts to fall, and compare with the datasheet

column1: 熱と定格を考える
column2: Thinking about heat and ratings

column1: 電圧差 × 電流 = 熱。放熱板が必要になる理由。定格チェックの見方
column2: Voltage difference × current = heat. Why a heatsink is needed. How to read the rating check

column1: 負荷を増やしながらレギュレータの温度を測り (触って確かめる前に、温度計で)、計算と比べます
column2: Measure the regulator's temperature while increasing the load (with a thermometer, before touching it), and compare with the calculation

column1: 発展: 熱にしない電源。リニアとの効率の違い
column2: Going further: supplies that don't waste power as heat. Efficiency compared with linear

column1: 電解コンデンサの寿命 (リップル電流と温度)
column2: Electrolytic capacitor life (ripple current and temperature)

column1: ESR の発熱で内部が温まる、寿命は 10℃ で半分、定格リップル電流を超えない
column2: ESR heating warms the inside, life halves every 10℃, don't exceed the rated ripple current

column1: 電解コンデンサを触って温度を感じ、データシートの定格リップルと寿命から、使う条件の寿命を見積もります
column2: Touch an electrolytic capacitor to feel its temperature, and estimate its life under your conditions from the datasheet's rated ripple and life

column1: ダイオードの逆回復 (切り替えの瞬間に逆向きに流れる)
column2: Diode reverse recovery (reverse current at the moment of switching)

column1: 順方向のとき貯めた電荷が抜けるまで逆向きに流れる、速い品とショットキー、スイッチング電源の損失とノイズ
column2: Current flows backwards until the charge stored in forward conduction is gone; fast types and Schottky; losses and noise in switching supplies

column1: 整流ダイオードの種類 (1N4007、高速、ショットキー) をデータシートの trr で見比べます
column2: Compare kinds of rectifier diodes (1N4007, fast, Schottky) by trr in their datasheets

column1: MOSFET のスイッチング損失 (ゲートの速さと熱)
column2: MOSFET switching loss (gate speed and heat)

column1: ゲート容量の充電で遅れる、ミラー期間、切り替え中の V × I が熱になる、損失 = 1 回あたりのエネルギー × 周波数
column2: Charging the gate capacitance causes delay, the Miller plateau, V × I during switching becomes heat, loss = energy per switch × frequency

column1: ゲート抵抗を変えて、ドレインの立ち下がりの速さと、MOSFET の温度の違いを見ます
column2: Change the gate resistor and see the difference in drain fall speed and MOSFET temperature

column1: リニアとスイッチングの比較 (熱にするか、貯めて運ぶか)
column2: Linear vs switching (turn it into heat, or store and carry it)

column1: リニアの効率 = 出力 ÷ 入力の電圧、損失は (Vin − Vout) × I、スイッチングは高い効率で、リップルと部品が増える
column2: Linear efficiency = output ÷ input voltage, loss is (Vin − Vout) × I; switching is highly efficient but adds ripple and parts

column1: 入力と出力の電圧と電流を測って、効率を計算し、リニアとスイッチングの温度を比べます
column2: Measure input and output voltage and current, calculate efficiency, and compare the temperatures of linear and switching

column1: オペアンプのスルーレート (出力が追いつけない速さ)
column2: Op-amp slew rate (how fast the output can follow)

column1: 出力の電圧の変化の速さには上限 (V/µs) がある、大きく速い信号は三角波にゆがむ、フルパワー帯域 = SR ÷ (2π Vp)
column2: The output voltage can only change so fast (V/µs); large, fast signals distort into triangles; full-power bandwidth = SR ÷ (2π Vp)

column1: オペアンプのボルテージフォロワに大きさと周波数を変えた正弦波を入れ、出力の形がゆがむ周波数を測ります
column2: Feed sine waves of different sizes and frequencies into an op-amp voltage follower, and measure the frequency where the output shape distorts

column1: EEPROM (I²C) の素顔 (オープンドレインとプルアップ)
column2: EEPROM (I²C) up close (open drain and pull-ups)

column1: バスは引き下げだけ・上げるのは抵抗、立ち上がり = 0.85 RC、プルアップの上限と下限、書き込みに数 ms
column2: The bus only pulls down, a resistor pulls up, rise time = 0.85 RC, upper and lower limits for the pull-up, writes take a few ms

column1: I²C のバス (SDA) をオシロで見て、プルアップの値を変えながら、立ち上がりの形を比べます
column2: Look at the I²C bus (SDA) on a scope and compare rise shapes while changing the pull-up value

column1: リレーやモータをつなぐ (フライバックダイオード)
column2: Connecting relays and motors (flyback diode)

column1: コイルの電流を急に切ると、大きな逆起電力が出てトランジスタを壊す。コイルと並列にダイオードを入れて止める
column2: Cutting a coil's current suddenly creates a large back EMF that destroys the transistor. A diode in parallel with the coil stops it

column1: リレー (または小さなモータ) をトランジスタで駆動し、ダイオードの向きを確かめます
column2: Drive a relay (or a small motor) with a transistor and check the diode's direction

column1: PWM とフィルタ (analogWrite でアナログ電圧を作る)
column2: PWM and filters (making an analog voltage with analogWrite)

column1: High と Low の割合 (デューティ) と RC フィルタで、途中の電圧を作る。揺れと反応の速さは引き換え。重い負荷には使えない
column2: The ratio of High to Low (duty) and an RC filter make an in-between voltage. Ripple and response speed are a trade-off. Not for heavy loads

column1: analogWrite の値を変えて、フィルタの出力をテスタで測ります
column2: Change the analogWrite value and measure the filter output with a multimeter

column1: 回路図から基板をつくる
column2: Making a board from a schematic

column1: 取り込み・配置・配線・DRC・発注の準備
column2: Import, placement, routing, DRC, preparing the order

column1: 発注するなら、少量・少額で試します
column2: If you order, try with a small quantity and low cost

column1: 配線の太さと電圧降下を確かめる
column2: Checking track width and voltage drop

column1: 細い配線で電圧が落ちるのをシミュレーションで見て、電流から必要な太さを決めて直す
column2: See in simulation how voltage drops on a thin track, then pick the needed width from the current and fix it

column1: 電源の入口と負荷のピンの電圧を、テスタで測って比べます (大きな電流を流すときは、配線や部品の発熱に注意します)
column2: Measure and compare the voltage at the supply input and at the load's pins with a multimeter (with large currents, watch for heating of tracks and parts)

column1: 発注前チェックをすべて通す (チャレンジ)
column2: Pass every pre-order check (challenge)

column1: 部品が基板の外・配線が切れている・配線が細い・発注先のルール違反、という基板を、チェックの表示を頼りに自分で直す
column2: Fix a board with parts outside the board, broken tracks, thin tracks and fab rule violations yourself, guided by what the check shows

column1: 発注の前に、発注先のページで最新の条件を必ず確かめます
column2: Before ordering, always check the latest conditions on the fab's website

column1: 基板にする: 置き方の勘所と配線
column2: Making it a board: placement tips and routing

column1: 水晶はマイコンのそば・バイパスコンデンサは電源ピンのそば。通らない線は、グリッドを細かくして直す。DRC と発注の準備まで
column2: Crystal next to the microcontroller, bypass capacitors next to the power pins. Fix lines that won't route by making the grid finer. Up to DRC and preparing the order

column1: USB の配線 (差動ペア)
column2: USB routing (differential pair)

column1: D+ と D− を並べて、同じ長さで、短く引く。差動ペアの機能と、長さの差の確かめ方
column2: Route D+ and D− side by side, the same length, and short. The differential pair feature and how to check the length difference

column1: 差動ペアどうしの長さを合わせる
column2: Matching lengths between differential pairs

column1: 2 レーンの差動信号を同時に届けるため、ペアどうしの長さを蛇行で揃える。2 本をいっしょに曲げるので、間隔が保たれる
column2: To deliver 2 lanes of differential signals at the same time, match the pairs' lengths with meanders. Both tracks bend together, so the spacing is kept

column1: 基板を手で仕上げる (自動配線で通らない線)
column2: Finishing a board by hand (lines autoroute can't route)

column1: 自動配置と自動配線のあと、18 本のネットが残った基板を、手で引く・ビアで渡す・邪魔な線を引き直す、で仕上げる。1 本通すごとに DRC を確かめる
column2: After autoplace and autoroute, finish a board with 18 nets left by routing by hand, crossing with vias and rerouting tracks in the way. Check DRC after each one you route

column1: 壊れた基板を直す (修理屋)
column2: Fixing a broken board (repair shop)

column1: ちゃんと動く基板に故障を 1 つ仕込み、症状から原因を探して直す。バイパスコンデンサが遠い・配線が切れている・細い・ショート・部品が基板の外。何度でも、別の故障で練習できる
column2: A fault is planted in a working board; find the cause from the symptoms and fix it. Bypass capacitor too far, broken track, thin track, short, part outside the board. Practice as often as you like with different faults

column1: MOSFET のスイッチ (ゲート電圧とオンの深さ)
column2: MOSFET switch (gate voltage and how fully it turns on)

column1: 電圧で駆動する。ゲート電圧がしきい値のあたりでオンになる。電流を流しすぎると発熱する
column2: Driven by voltage. It turns on when the gate voltage is around the threshold. Too much current makes it heat up

column1: PNP のハイサイドスイッチ (電源側で入り切り)
column2: PNP high-side switch (switching on the supply side)

column1: NPN と逆に、入力を Low にするとオンになる。ベース抵抗の大きさが、オンの深さを決める
column2: Opposite to NPN, it turns on when the input is Low. The base resistor value decides how fully it turns on

column1: リチウムイオン電池の充電 (TP4056)
column2: Charging a lithium-ion battery (TP4056)

column1: 充電の 3 段階 (予備充電・定電流・定電圧)。IC の内部は見ず、外から見た動きで確かめる
column2: The 3 charging stages (pre-charge, constant current, constant voltage). Check the behavior from outside without looking inside the IC

column1: オペアンプで信号を大きくする (非反転増幅)
column2: Amplifying a signal with an op-amp (non-inverting amplifier)

column1: 帰還の考え方。抵抗の比がゲインを決める
column2: The idea of feedback. The resistor ratio sets the gain

column1: オペアンプの増幅回路を作り、入力と出力をテスタやオシロで測ります
column2: Build an op-amp amplifier and measure input and output with a multimeter or scope

column1: オペアンプの反転増幅 (仮想接地)
column2: Op-amp inverting amplifier (virtual ground)

column1: 反転入力が 0V に保たれる仕組み
column2: How the inverting input is held at 0V

column1: 高い周波数だけを弱める。カットオフ周波数は 1 ÷ (2π R C)。抵抗とコンデンサの値で決まる
column2: Weakens only high frequencies. The cutoff frequency is 1 ÷ (2π R C), set by the resistor and capacitor values

column1: 行き過ぎとリンギング (RLC 回路)
column2: Overshoot and ringing (RLC circuit)

column1: コイルとコンデンサの回路は、ステップに対して行き過ぎて揺れる。抵抗で抑える
column2: A coil-and-capacitor circuit overshoots and oscillates after a step. A resistor damps it

column1: 使い回したい回路を別のシートに1つ描き、記号 (箱) にして何回も置く。中を直すと全部に効く。コピーごとに部品とネットの名前が別になる
column2: Draw a circuit you want to reuse once on a separate sheet, make it a symbol (box) and place it many times. Fixing the inside fixes them all. Each copy gets its own part and net names

column1: 555 で LED を点滅させる
column2: Blinking an LED with a 555

column1: タイマー IC とコンデンサの充放電で、一定の間隔で点滅する。C や R を変えると、周期が変わる
column2: A timer IC and a capacitor charging and discharging make it blink at a steady interval. Changing C or R changes the period

column1: 極と零 (RLC の共振を式で見る)
column2: Poles and zeros (RLC resonance as equations)

column1: 山の位置は極の周波数、鋭さは Q。抵抗を大きくすると、極が実数になって山が消える
column2: The peak's position is the pole frequency, its sharpness is Q. A larger resistor makes the poles real and the peak disappears

column1: ノイズ解析 (増幅回路の雑音はどこから来る)
column2: Noise analysis (where an amplifier's noise comes from)

column1: 抵抗の熱雑音とトランジスタのショット雑音を、部品ごとに分けて見る。信号源の抵抗を小さくすると減る
column2: See resistor thermal noise and transistor shot noise part by part. A lower source resistance reduces it

column1: 位相余裕 (容量の負荷でオペアンプが不安定になる)
column2: Phase margin (a capacitive load makes an op-amp unstable)

column1: ゲインが 0dB になる周波数で、180° に対する余裕。出力の容量負荷が、余裕を食う
column2: The margin to 180° at the frequency where the gain is 0dB. A capacitive load on the output eats into the margin

column1: 安定化電源を作ろう
column2: Build a regulated power supply

column1: ACアダプタや電池の電圧を、負荷が変わっても一定の 5V にする電源を、原理から理解して、回路図・基板・実機まで自分で作ります。実験は、安全のため 12V 以下の低い電圧だけで行います
column2: Understand from first principles a supply that turns an AC adapter's or battery's voltage into a steady 5V even when the load changes, and build it yourself: schematic, board and real hardware. For safety, experiments use only low voltages of 12V or less

column1: 1. 入門: 電圧・電流と測り方
column2: 1. Intro: voltage, current and how to measure them

column1: 電圧を分ける、電流を制限する、電池が負荷で電圧を下げる。安定化電源が「何を一定にするのか」の土台です
column2: Dividing voltage, limiting current, a battery's voltage dropping under load. The basis of "what a regulated supply keeps steady"

column1: 電圧を分ける (分圧回路)
column2: Dividing voltage (voltage divider)

column1: 抵抗2本で好きな電圧を作る。出力が負荷で変わる理由の入口
column2: Make any voltage with 2 resistors. A first look at why the output changes with the load

column1: テスタで電圧を測る。抵抗2本をブレッドボードにつなぎ、計算値と測定値を比べます
column2: Measure voltage with a multimeter. Connect 2 resistors on a breadboard and compare calculated and measured values

column1: 電流を決めるのは抵抗。電流を測る方法も
column2: The resistor decides the current. Plus how to measure current

column1: LED の電流をテスタの電流レンジで測り、抵抗を変えて明るさと電流を比べます
column2: Measure an LED's current on the multimeter's current range, and compare brightness and current while changing the resistor

column1: 2. 基礎: 電源をつくる部品
column2: 2. Basics: parts that make a supply

column1: ダイオード・コンデンサ・ツェナー・トランジスタ。電圧を整え、ならし、一定にし、電流を増やす部品の働きです

column1: バリスタの素顔 (電圧が高くなると導通して守る)
column2: Varistors up close (conducting at high voltage to protect)

column1: V ∝ I^(1/α) の曲線、動作電圧の手前の漏れ、サージを吸収して制限電圧に止める、劣化
column2: The V ∝ I^(1/α) curve, leakage below the operating voltage, absorbing surges and clamping at the limit voltage, wear-out

column1: バリスタの抵抗を測り、定格の連続電圧が回路の電圧より十分高いことを、データシートで確かめます (サージを実際に加える実験はしません)
column2: Measure a varistor's resistance and check in the datasheet that its rated continuous voltage is well above the circuit voltage (no experiment applies real surges)

column1: 6. スイッチ・時計・音・ロジック
column2: 6. Switches, clocks, sound, logic

column1: コイルで動くリレー、周波数を決める水晶、音を出すスピーカーとブザー、High と Low を扱うロジック IC
column2: Relays moved by a coil, crystals that set frequency, speakers and buzzers that make sound, logic ICs that handle High and Low

column1: スイッチの素顔 (閉じた接点は小さな抵抗)
column2: Switches up close (a closed contact is a small resistance)

column1: 接点抵抗と電圧降下・発熱、小さな電流の信号には金メッキ、定格と寿命
column2: Contact resistance with voltage drop and heating, gold plating for small signal currents, ratings and life

column1: スイッチを閉じた状態の抵抗を測り、押すたびに変わるか、電流を流して電圧降下を見ます
column2: Measure the resistance of a closed switch, see whether it changes with each press, and pass current to see the voltage drop

column1: アナログスイッチの素顔 (オン抵抗と、サンプル用のコンデンサ)
column2: Analog switches up close (on-resistance, and the sampling capacitor)

column1: オン抵抗 Ron の分圧誤差、オフ時の漏れが小さい、サンプルホールドの時定数 (Rs + Ron) × C
column2: Divider error from on-resistance Ron, low leakage when off, sample-and-hold time constant (Rs + Ron) × C

column1: アナログスイッチ IC で信号を通し、負荷の抵抗を変えて、電圧の下がりを測ります
column2: Pass a signal through an analog switch IC, change the load resistance, and measure the voltage drop

column1: リレーの素顔 (コイルの電流で接点が動く)
column2: Relays up close (the coil's current moves the contacts)

column1: コイル = 抵抗 + インダクタンス、動作電圧 (定格の約 75%)、τ = L ÷ R、電力 V² ÷ R
column2: Coil = resistance + inductance, pull-in voltage (about 75% of rated), τ = L ÷ R, power V² ÷ R

column1: 5V 用リレーのコイルの抵抗を測り、電圧を上げながらカチッと動作する電圧を探します
column2: Measure the coil resistance of a 5V relay, and raise the voltage to find where it clicks on

column1: 水晶の素顔 (Q が桁違いに大きい共振)
column2: Crystals up close (resonance with an enormously high Q)

column1: 等価回路 Rm・Lm・Cm・C0、fs = 1 ÷ (2π√(Lm Cm))、Q = ωL ÷ R、帯域幅 = fs ÷ Q
column2: Equivalent circuit Rm, Lm, Cm, C0, fs = 1 ÷ (2π√(Lm Cm)), Q = ωL ÷ R, bandwidth = fs ÷ Q

column1: 水晶を LC 共振回路と並べ、ふつうの LC より山が桁違いに細いことを、発振器の周波数の安定として確かめます
column2: Put a crystal next to an LC resonant circuit and confirm, as oscillator frequency stability, that its peak is orders of magnitude narrower than an ordinary LC

column1: スピーカーとブザーの素顔 (インピーダンスは 8Ω 一定ではない)
column2: Speakers and buzzers up close (impedance isn't a constant 8Ω)

column1: 共振で上がるインピーダンス、高い周波数でコイルとして上がる、圧電ブザーは容量+共振
column2: Impedance rises at resonance and rises at high frequencies as a coil; a piezo buzzer is capacitance + resonance

column1: スピーカーのインピーダンスを、テスタで測る直流の抵抗 (約 8Ω ではなく 6〜7Ω) と、アンプの表示を比べます
column2: Compare a speaker's DC resistance measured with a multimeter (6-7Ω, not about 8Ω) with the rating printed on it

column1: ロジック IC の素顔 (しきい値・ヒステリシス・出力の力)
column2: Logic ICs up close (threshold, hysteresis, output drive)

column1: しきい値は電源の半分、シュミットトリガは 0.6 / 0.4 Vcc、出力は電源につながる約 60Ω の抵抗
column2: The threshold is half the supply, a Schmitt trigger is 0.6 / 0.4 Vcc, the output is about a 60Ω resistance to the supply

column1: 74HC04 と 74HC14 にゆっくり変わる信号とノイズを入れ、出力が揺れるか確かめます
column2: Feed slowly changing signals and noise into a 74HC04 and a 74HC14, and see whether the output chatters

column1: 信号を扱おう: フィルタ・増幅・発振
column2: Working with signals: filters, amplifiers, oscillators

column1: 周波数ごとに信号を弱める (フィルタ)、大きくする (増幅)、自分で振動させる (発振) を、AC 解析と過渡解析で見ます。山の正体 (極と Q) と、増幅が不安定になる理由 (位相余裕) まで、原理から理解します。
column2: See in AC and transient analysis how to weaken signals by frequency (filters), make them larger (amplifiers) and make them oscillate by themselves (oscillators). Understand from first principles what a peak really is (poles and Q) and why amplifiers become unstable (phase margin).

column1: 1. フィルタ
column2: 1. Filters

column1: 抵抗とコンデンサで高い周波数を弱める。コイルを足すと、行き過ぎて揺れる。その山を、極と零で読む
column2: A resistor and capacitor weaken high frequencies. Adding a coil makes it overshoot and ring. Read that peak with poles and zeros

column1: 2. 増幅と安定
column2: 2. Amplifying and stability

column1: オペアンプの帰還でゲインを決める。出力に容量をつなぐと、位相余裕が減って不安定になる
column2: Op-amp feedback sets the gain. A capacitance on the output reduces the phase margin and makes it unstable

column1: 3. 発振
column2: 3. Oscillators

column1: コンデンサの充放電で、自分で一定の間隔を作る
column2: Make a steady interval by yourself with a capacitor charging and discharging
